title: Osero's Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is levied on market capitalization rather than on revenue or profit
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.3.1.2.1.1.1 sets the entire terms of Osero's Ecosystem Upkeep Fee in one line: "Osero will pay 0.50% of its market capitalization per year in USDS."

The choice of base is the substance. A market-cap fee is a tax on valuation, not on activity. It is trivially verifiable from public data and cannot be reduced by accounting choices about what counts as revenue or cost — the classic weakness of profit-based arrangements between an ecosystem and its operating entities.

The cost is that the obligation is uncorrelated with the Agent's ability to pay. An Osero whose token trades high while its lending book earns little owes more, not less; an Osero that is profitable but out of favour owes less. The fee also grows automatically with market enthusiasm, so a token rally raises the Agent's operating cost.

Denomination in USDS is a second, separable decision. Paying the ecosystem's own stablecoin means every Prime Agent must continuously source USDS to stay current, turning the upkeep obligation into structural, recurring demand for the very asset the ecosystem issues — payment discipline and monetary policy in the same instrument.
description: 0.50% of market cap per year, payable in USDS: the obligation scales with the token market's valuation of the Agent, not with what the Agent actually earns.
